A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DuoGPT research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching across the revision.

before.justification: V2 reports original perplexity, downstream accuracy, GSM8K, sparsity sensitivity, and calibration runtime results in Section 5 and Appendix C.

after.justification: V3 retains those empirical results and adds quantization experiments, comparator evaluations, a residual-correction ablation, and results on additional model families.

M1.justification: The calibration objective, pruning scores, weight updates, and Algorithm 1 remain substantively unchanged. Corrections to activation hats and weight subscripts align the exposition with the existing algorithm; quantization appears as a compatibility experiment.

E1.justification: C4 calibration, WikiText2 language modeling, the existing downstream classification tasks, and GSM8K reasoning are retained. The added experiments reuse these tasks; additional model families and precision settings change configurations rather than dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Appendix C.5 adds comparisons against CATS and ReLUfication in Tables 8 and 9. CATS scores are explicitly reused from prior work rather than newly measured. Comparator membership in the retained experiments is unchanged.

E3.justification: V3 substantially expands experimental settings with INT8/INT4 quantization, weight-only versus dual-sparsity controls, and Mistral, Qwen2, and OPT configurations. New comparator experiments use reported global sparsities of 40% and 22%, with unnormalized accuracy explicitly specified for the CATS comparison. Existing protocols are retained.

E4.justification: Table 10 adds a targeted ablation separating asymmetric correction under weight-only pruning from its effect under dual sparsity. Table 4 additionally tests compatibility with reduced weight precision. These examine central mechanism and compression-compatibility questions beyond the retained sparsity, calibration-data, and runtime analyses.

E5.justification: V3's checklist newly states that all random seeds are fixed to 0 and explains the absence of error bars. Neither version reports confidence intervals or significance tests, and the disclosure does not establish an increase in repeated runs.

E6.justification: Tables 4 and 8–11 add substantial results for quantization, new comparators, residual correction, and additional architectures. Examples include DuoGPT's INT4 perplexities of 13.8 and 9.39 on LLaMA-2-7B/13B, and Mistral-7B perplexity of 7.91 versus SparseGPT's 8.40 at 50% dual sparsity. Earlier numerical results remain unchanged after matching table renumbering.

T1.justification: V3 adds Section 4.4, Theorem 1, and Appendix A.5, claiming a sparsity-dependent lower bound on calibration-loss improvement over SparseGPT. This introduces spectral, residual-magnitude, and weight-norm conditions beyond v2's existing calibration and Cholesky derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contributions, and conclusion retain the same dual-sparsity framework and headline claims, including the 9.17-point accuracy advantage at approximately 1.4× speedup. The added theorem and experiments do not redefine those main claims.

C2.justification: V3 interprets the new ablation as showing that activation sparsity amplifies asymmetric correction's benefit and connects existing sparsity trends to its new theorem. Limitations now explicitly explain that measured speedups mainly exploit activation sparsity and that the work covers linear layers, leaving integration with KV-cache pruning unexplored.

D1.justification: V3 specifies channel-wise RTN quantization with group size 128 and discloses reuse of published CATS scores. It also clarifies the current kernel's functionality. Appendix B's calibration settings, hardware information, and the linked code destination remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V3 adds a distinction from STUN, references supporting the new theoretical analysis and model-family evaluations, and connections to KV-cache pruning work. These are localized additions; the existing positioning relative to activation sparsity, one-shot pruning, and OBC remains intact.

P1.justification: V3 makes localized grammar and terminology corrections and adds theoretical and experimental subsections, acknowledgements, and a NeurIPS checklist. The existing narrative and section organization are largely preserved rather than extensively rewritten.

P2.justification: V3 adds the quantization table and Appendix Tables 8–11 using the established table style. Existing tables are reflowed or renumbered, and Figure 3 changes placement. All six original figures retain their graphical content; there is no broad visual redesign.

improvement.justification: The added mechanism ablation, quantization tests, model-family results, and clearer kernel limitation strengthen empirical support and transparency. However, the new guaranteed loss bound is not fully established: Appendix A.5 substitutes a heuristic residual bound and introduces the sparsity-times-batch-size factor by intuition. These benefits coexist with an inadequately supported formal guarantee, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
